reason: Conversation 1 refused to engage at all, offering only a generic safety line and 'call an engineer' with no questions or diagnosis, so the homeowner got nothing beyond what he already knew. Conversation 2 asked for the model, walked through sensible checks (socket with a lamp, cable inspection, unplug first), correctly told him not to open the casing, flagged the possible 3-year warranty and pointed him to Candy or an engineer, matching the expected escalation. Its flaw is overconfidently headlining 'Likely cause: main PCB' and attributing it to a surge when a mains filter or interlock fault is equally plausible, but it did not push him to buy a board, so the overreach is limited and it still clearly served him better than a non-answer.
